metadata.title: Construct Binary Tree from Inorder and Postorder Traversal

problem_summary.summary: Reconstruct the unique tree represented by matching inorder and postorder traversals.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: inorder and postorder arrays of the same tree. Return its root.
constraints: Both arrays are valid traversals of the same tree

brute_force.explanation: Take the last postorder value as each subtree root, linearly locate it in the current inorder interval, then recursively build the two resulting intervals.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Postorder ends with the subtree root, and its inorder position divides that subtree into exactly its left and right parts.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n^2) worst case due to repeated linear searches in inorder.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(h) auxiliary recursion stack, excluding the returned tree.

optimized.explanation: Map each inorder value to its index, then use postorder interval boundaries to construct subtrees without scanning for splits.
optimized.correctness_idea: For each interval, the final postorder element is its root. The mapped inorder index gives the left-subtree size, which partitions the remaining postorder segment correctly.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) expected — indexing, construction, and each map lookup take expected linear total time.
optimized.space_complexity: O(n) for the index map and output tree, plus O(h) recursion stack.

steps.event: Select the final postorder value as root.
steps.condition: Inorder index 3 leaves three values to the left and none to the right.
steps.action: Create root 9 and build its left interval.

steps.condition: Inorder values [2] and [7] are the left and right intervals.
Each selected interval contains one item.
steps.action: Create both leaf nodes and return the completed tree.

edge_cases.handling: The value becomes the sole leaf.
The inorder split produces an empty interval on the missing side.
Construction remains correct, with recursion depth proportional to node count.
